definition.en: A conceptual label to characterise the unequal power relations between men as a group and women as a group.

en: Rooted in Western thought since Ancient Greece, male dominance has historically justified the exclusion of women from the public sphere and the elevation of masculine traits over feminine ones, often by claiming that such social hierarchies are a natural and desirable consequence of biological differences. Therefore, it refers to a social system in which power is systematically distributed in favour of men, and where what counts as neutral, objective, or universal is in fact defined by male standards. Gender differences thus emerge not as natural facts, but as outcomes of this asymmetrical distribution of power.
